owner.newOwnerLabel: New owner (must already be a member of this tenant)
owner.noCandidates: No other admins on this tenant. Invite one via AgriPulse → Settings → Users first.
owner.assignIntro: Seed the first TenantOwner — invite a new user or promote an existing tenant member.

guard.forbiddenBody: You don't have permission to manage tenants. Sign in with a PlatformAdmin account.

list.empty: No tenants yet. Create the first one to get started.

create.subtitle: Provision a tenant with an initial owner.

fields.slugHelp: URL-safe identifier, 3–32 chars, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens. Permanent.
fields.name: Display name
fields.ownerEmailHelp: Required. The TenantOwner is provisioned in Keycloak and assigned the role at creation.

errors.slugConflict: A tenant with this slug already exists.
errors.contactEmailInvalid: Contact email must be a valid address.
errors.ownerEmailInvalid: Owner email must be a valid address.

review.ownerNote: An UPDATE_PASSWORD email will be sent to {{email}}.
review.noOwnerNote: No owner specified — Keycloak provisioning is skipped. You can complete it later via the retry endpoint.

success.title: Tenant created
success.noOwner: Tenant ready. Provision the Keycloak owner manually or via the retry endpoint when ready.
success.pendingProvision: Tenant created, but Keycloak provisioning failed. Use 'Retry provisioning' on the detail page once the issue is resolved.

detail.title: Tenant detail
detail.subtitle: Profile, settings, and lifecycle actions.
detail.comingSoon: Lifecycle actions (suspend / reactivate / delete / purge) will appear here in PR-F.

banner.suspended: This tenant is suspended. Sign-ins are blocked.
banner.pending_delete: This tenant is marked for deletion. Purge eligible {{when}}.
banner.pending_provision: Provisioning pending — Keycloak invite hasn't completed yet.

suspend.title: Suspend tenant
suspend.body: Sign-ins for this tenant will be blocked within ~30 seconds. Existing data is preserved.

requestDelete.title: Mark tenant for deletion
requestDelete.body: Starts the {{days}}-day grace window. After that, the tenant can be hard-purged. Cancellation returns the tenant to suspended.

purge.title: Purge tenant — irreversible
purge.body: This will DROP SCHEMA the tenant, delete public rows, and remove the Keycloak group + users. There is no undo.
purge.forceWarning: Use only when authorised — bypasses the {{days}}-day cooling-off period.

backfill.title: Backfill
backfill.subtitle: Load historical imagery and weather for a farm, and compute indices over data already stored.
backfill.started: Run started. Follow it on the Runs tab.

hint.imagery: Sentinel-2 scenes from CDSE. Raw bands only. Consumes processing units.
hint.weather: Hourly observations from the Open-Meteo archive. Free, no quota.
hint.imageryIndices: NDVI, NDMI, NDRE, SAVI, EVI, NDWI and GNDVI, recomputed per stored scene.
hint.weatherIndices: GDD, ET₀ and rainfall accumulations projected into daily weather indices.
hint.rawOnly: Backfill loads raw data only. Compute indices afterwards from the Indices tab.
hint.indicesFree: Runs over data already stored — no provider calls and no processing units.

estimate.title: Before you run this
estimate.units: Roughly {{units}} processing units. This is an estimate, not a quota reading.
estimate.farmAoi: This farm is fetched as one whole-farm area, so the imagery run pulls one surface per pass and measures every block off it — the same shape as its live data.
estimate.noImagerySubs: This farm has no active imagery subscriptions — an imagery backfill would fetch nothing. Configure them on the farm first.
estimate.noWeatherSubs: This farm has no active weather subscriptions — a weather backfill would fetch nothing. Configure them on the farm first.

dialog.irreversible: This cannot be undone. Archiving is reversible — purging is not.
dialog.previewError: Could not load the impact report.
dialog.submitError: The purge could not be started.
dialog.dryRunStillOk: You can still run a dry run — it changes nothing.

blockedShort.tenant_not_suspended: Tenant is active — suspend it first.

result.dryRunTitle: Dry run complete — nothing was deleted

data.resetAllHint: Removes every farm and block and all their data. Keeps the tenant, its users, settings and integration keys. Requires the tenant to be suspended first.
data.loadError: Could not load this tenant's farms.

orphans.title: Orphaned data
orphans.hint: Rows and schemas left behind by earlier deletions. Read-only — scanning changes nothing.
orphans.straySchemas: Tenant schemas with no tenant row: {{schemas}}

cropAttrs.title: Attributes — {{crop}}
cropAttrs.subtitle: Typed fields that appear on this crop's block assignments. Definitions resolve deepest-wins across crop → variety → strain.
cropAttrs.previewHint: This is the form a user sees. Change a gating answer to watch the gated fields appear.
cropAttrs.previewEmpty: Define an attribute to see the form it produces.
cropAttrs.empty: No attributes defined for this crop yet.
cropAttrs.attachHelp: Attach deeper to override an inherited definition of the same code.
cropAttrs.groupHelp: Fields sharing a group render together under one heading.
cropAttrs.gateNeedsValue: Pick at least one value, or the gate never opens.
cropAttrs.noGateTargets: No single-choice or yes/no field to gate on yet.

err.code: Use letters, numbers, _ or -, up to 32 characters.
err.reserved: This code is already a built-in field. Pick another.
err.optionCode: Every option needs a valid code.
err.optionNames: Every option needs an English and an Arabic name.

observer.title: Observer
observer.subtitle: End-to-end view of the indices pipeline: raw scenes, per-pixel maths, cell and block aggregates, trends, and what they produced.
observer.pickFarmFirst: Pick a tenant and a farm to begin. Observer is farm-scoped — the pipeline only means something against a specific set of blocks.
observer.trendAmbiguous: This farm holds aggregates from more than one product. The daily trend rollup has no product dimension, so trend coverage cannot be attributed to the selected product alone.
observer.consumersProxy: Consumers are counted by creation time in this window, not by proven descent from these scenes.
observer.mixedCalcVersions: Two calculation versions in this window — the trend line mixes methodologies

rail.title: Selection
rail.noScenes: No scenes have ever been ingested for this farm.

diagnosis.generic: {{count}} of {{expected}} expected outputs are missing at this stage.
diagnosis.acquired: {{count}} scene(s) were discovered but never downloaded. Check the provider errors in the scene list.
diagnosis.indices: {{count}} scene(s) downloaded successfully but wrote no aggregates — the job reads as succeeded because the download succeeded, so index computation is where they died.
diagnosis.cells: {{count}} scene(s) on gridded blocks produced no cell aggregates. Blocks with no grid governing the scene's time are already excluded from this count.
diagnosis.trend: {{count}} block-day(s) have aggregates but no daily-trend bucket. The trend rollup refreshes on a rolling window, so history written outside it stays invisible until a manual refresh.

scenes.title: Scenes
scenes.loadFailed: Couldn't load the scenes for this selection. This is a failed request, not an empty result — retry, or narrow the date range.
scenes.noAggregates: This scene wrote no index aggregates.

tooltip.cloudPct: Cloud cover across the whole scene as reported by the provider — not measured for this block specifically.
tooltip.validPct: Valid pixels divided by the block's pixel footprint. A low value means the number came from a fraction of the field.
tooltip.indices: How many of the product's supported indices wrote an aggregate row for this scene.

pixel.title: Pixel inspector
pixel.clickPrompt: Click a pixel on the raster to see the bands that went in, the masking decision, and the arithmetic that produced its value.
pixel.error: Could not read that pixel. It may fall outside the scene's raster.
pixel.noMaskBand: This product ships no scene-classification band, so no cloud masking ran. Its valid-pixel share is not comparable to a product that does mask.
pixel.outsideAoi: Outside the block boundary — this pixel is not aggregated.
pixel.excluded: Excluded from every statistic on this scene: {{reason}}.
pixel.contributes: This pixel contributes to the cell and block aggregates.

budget.title: Pixel budget
budget.explain: Where this scene's pixels went. The database stores only the valid and total counts, so this is recomputed from the stored raster — one read, on request.
budget.noIndex: No budget for {{index}} on this scene.
budget.notStored: Not stored today: the split between cloud-masked and no-data pixels is recomputed live. OBS-5 persists it.

detail.raster: Index raster — click a pixel to explain it
detail.noRaster: This scene never produced a raster, so there is nothing to inspect.
detail.noGrid: No grid governed this scene's time — no cell aggregates are expected.
detail.rollupNote: Cell means and the block mean are computed over different lattices, so they reconcile approximately rather than exactly — the block mean covers every pixel in the boundary, while cells partition it on a fixed grid.
detail.overwritten: This scene was recomputed under a different calculation version
detail.noHistory: No calculation runs recorded for this scene. Lineage is only written for scenes computed after this feature shipped.

verify.title: Verify this scene
verify.failed: Verification could not run. The scene's raster may be unreadable.
verify.explainFull: Reads the raw bands and re-runs the AOI mask, the cloud mask and every formula, then compares against the stored numbers. The only mode that can catch a masking-rule change.
verify.explainFast: Recomputes from the per-index rasters the pipeline already wrote. Cheaper, but masking is baked into those files — a match here confirms the summary, not the masking.
verify.neverRepairs: Observer never repairs. Nothing was written to the pipeline's tables — a drift verdict is a signal, and the fix is a re-run from the Backfill Console, which owns provider quota and progress reporting.

runs.title: Verification runs
runs.explain: Anything wider than one scene is a named run: a year across 36 blocks is roughly 2,500 recomputations. One run per farm, with progress and a cancel.
runs.conflict: This farm already has a verification in progress. Cancel it first, or wait for it to finish.
runs.empty: No verification runs for this farm yet.

weather.farmScoped: Weather is measured at one point per farm, so blocks do not apply here. The block picker is disabled rather than silently ignored.
weather.title: Weather
weather.notSubscribed: This farm has no weather subscription, so every count below would be zero because nothing was ever configured — not because anything is broken.
weather.coverageExplain: How many of each day's 24 hours actually arrived. This is the weather equivalent of valid-pixel percentage: a day below {{floor}} hours produces a confident-looking daily value computed from a fraction of the day.
weather.noFloor: The derivation applies no coverage floor of its own — thin days below are reported, not rejected. Nothing downstream knows the difference.
weather.noObservations: No hourly observations in this window.
weather.noIndexRow: No daily index row for that day.
weather.noAttempts: No fetch attempts in this window.

lineage.title: What {{index}} produced
lineage.explain: Alerts and recommendations whose conditions actually read this index, with the value each one saw. These are stored edges recorded by the decision engine, not decisions that merely happened nearby in time.
lineage.none: Nothing on this block read this index in this window.
lineage.threshold: Threshold z = {{k}} (source: {{source}}). The tenant-level setting is not re-resolved here, so a module default is not necessarily the number the nightly sweep used.

cells.title: Cells
cells.prompt: Click a cell on the map to see the pixels it was aggregated from. Click anywhere else to inspect a single pixel.
cells.truncated: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} pixels — the block is larger than the map cap, so this is a prefix, not the whole field.
cells.howAggregated: How the cell value is computed
cells.noStoredRow: no stored aggregate for this cell
cells.membership: Cell and block counts do not sum, by design: a cell claims a pixel when the pixel's centre falls inside it, while the block claims a pixel when its footprint touches the boundary. Edge pixels therefore count for the block but for no cell.
cells.legend: Pixel fill shows the index value; grey pixels carry no usable value. Blue outlines are grid cells — dashed where the cell has no stored aggregate. The red outline is the block boundary.

signals.title: Signal catalog
signals.subtitle: Platform-curated signal definitions and forms. Every tenant reads these; a tenant that defines the same code overrides it for itself only.
signals.loadFailed: Could not load the signal catalog.

phenology.heading: Stage calendar — {{crop}}
phenology.perennialHint: A perennial has no planting date to count from, so stages advance on calendar windows (MM-DD, and a window may wrap past new year).
phenology.annualHint: An annual counts from its planting date, in days or in accumulated growing degree days.
phenology.empty: No stages yet. Until this crop has a calendar, its blocks can never advance a growth stage — and any decision tree that gates on one will never fire for them.
phenology.needsGddBase: This crop has no GDD base temperature, so a degree-day stage can never resolve. Set one on the crop first.

catalog.title: Crop catalog console
catalog.subtitle: Select a node on the left; everything about it — settings, stage ladder, size classes and attributes — is described on the right. Stage ladders and size classes resolve deepest-wins across crop → variety → strain, and an override replaces the level above it whole.
catalog.pickNode: Pick a crop, variety or strain on the left.
catalog.depthHint: How deep a block assignment must classify: the crop alone, down to a variety, or down to a strain.
catalog.gddBaseHint: Required before any stage can advance on degree days.
catalog.gddUpperHint: Optional. Caps how much a hot day can contribute.
catalog.gddPerennialNote: A perennial advances on calendar windows, so degree days don't apply to it.
catalog.relevantIndicesHint: Which remote-sensing indices this crop surfaces.
catalog.nodeSettingsNote: A variety or strain carries no agronomic settings of its own — everything else it can hold is an override of the crop's, on the tabs above.
catalog.stagesOwned: This node defines its own stage ladder.
catalog.stagesMissing: No level of this taxonomy defines a stage ladder, so blocks classified here can never advance a growth stage — and any decision tree gated on one will never fire for them.
catalog.sizesOwned: This node defines its own size classes.
catalog.sizesMissing: No level of this taxonomy defines canopy size classes, so the block's size dropdown has nothing to offer.
catalog.ownExplainer: It replaces the level above it whole.
catalog.inheritedExplainer: Editing it here would rewrite it for everything else inheriting from {{from}}. Create an override to change it for this node alone.
catalog.copyWarning: Starting from a copy of the {{count}} inherited from {{from}}. Saving replaces the inherited value whole for this node — an override never merges.
catalog.emptyOverrideWarning: Nothing is inherited here, so this starts empty.
catalog.attrsScope: The typed fields a block classified at {{path}} receives.
catalog.attrsNoneAttached: No attribute is attached at this node.
catalog.createDefaults: Starts as a crop-only annual with no calendar. Set the cycle, the classification depth and the degree-day temperatures on Details afterwards.

sizeClasses.hint: The canopy sizes offered on a block's crop assignment. Order is taken from position.
sizeClasses.empty: No size classes yet, so the block's size dropdown has nothing to offer.

roles.title: Roles & permissions
roles.subtitle: Every role in the platform and the permissions it grants. Read-only — the policy ships with the release.
roles.loadFailed: Could not load the roles and permissions.
roles.subtitleCounts: {{roles}} roles · {{permissions}} permissions · {{enforced}} enforced · {{pending}} not yet enforced
roles.tableCaptionRoles: Roles — select one to see its permissions
roles.tipGranted: Whether this role grants the permission. A tick means a user with only this role passes the check.
roles.tipScope: Which layer of the token can grant this permission — platform, tenant, or a single farm. Documentation only: the resolver enforces the role mapping, not this field.
roles.tipStatus: Enforced means a live endpoint checks this permission today. Pending means it is reserved for a module that has not shipped, so granting it has no effect yet.
roles.tipTier: The layer the role is defined at. Platform roles are cross-tenant, tenant roles cover every farm in a tenant, farm roles are granted per farm.
roles.tipHolders: Distinct people holding this role right now, across all tenants. Someone scoped to five farms counts once.
roles.tipGrantedTo: Every role that grants this permission. A user holding any of them passes the check.

edit.editableDetail: Select a tick or dash in the Granted column to grant or revoke a permission. Every change is confirmed first and recorded in the change log.
edit.editableHint: You can change what {{role}} is allowed to do.
edit.emptyChanges: No permissions have been changed. Every role is at its shipped default.
edit.propagation: Takes effect immediately here and on every other server within {{seconds}} seconds. Signed-in users keep their existing session.
edit.saveFailed: Could not apply the change. Nothing was saved — try again.
edit.stubDetail: No route checks it today, so granting it changes nothing until the feature ships. It is recorded and will apply once it does.
edit.tableCaptionChanges: Every runtime permission change, newest first
edit.tipDefault: Whether this permission still matches the value AgriPulse ships. Edited permissions stay edited across deploys until you reset them.
edit.wildcardImmutable: PlatformAdmin grants every permission and cannot be edited. That is enforced by the server, so nobody can remove the access needed to undo a mistake made on this page.
